scenes.title: DELETE
scenes.narration: DELETE removes rows from a table, guided by a WHERE clause that targets exactly what to erase.

scenes.title: Removing rows
bullets: WHERE selects which rows to delete
Omitting WHERE clears the whole table
scenes.narration: DELETE removes the rows that match its WHERE condition from a table. If you omit WHERE, every row is deleted, leaving the table empty. Either way, the table's structure and definition stay firmly in place.

scenes.title: Deleting specific rows
scenes.narration: This statement removes only the orders whose status is cancelled. The WHERE clause pinpoints exactly which rows should disappear. Every other order remains untouched in the table.

scenes.heading: DELETE vs TRUNCATE
scenes.narration: DELETE is precise, using a WHERE clause to remove just the rows you specify. TRUNCATE is faster but blunt, clearing the entire table at once with no filter. Pick DELETE for selective removals and TRUNCATE for a complete, rapid reset.

scenes.text: Use DELETE with a careful WHERE clause to remove exactly the rows you intend and nothing more.
scenes.narration: Always pair DELETE with a precise WHERE clause so you erase only the intended rows, since an unfiltered DELETE empties the table.
